reviews.title: Great app but shadow bans without reason
reviews.text:
I genuinely love Bumpy, developers. I truly do, and I hope you keep that in mind as you read this review.

Unfortunately, I've been experiencing a serious issue with my account, and I cannot determine whether I've been shadowbanned or if there's a significant bug affecting my profile.

I've reached out to the developers multiple times via email, only to be told that nothing is wrong with my account. Very helpful.

To investigate this further, I contacted someone I had originally matched with on Bumpy and later connected with outside the app. They agreed to help me test the issue.

While sharing their screen with me in real time, I sent them messages through Bumpy. Not a single message appeared on their end, despite appearing to send successfully on mine. Even more concerning, they could no longer find my profile.

I carefully documented everything, gathered evidence, and sent a detailed report to the developers, including information about how to reproduce the issue. As someone familiar with web development, I understand how difficult bugs can be to identify and resolve. I genuinely wanted to help the team investigate and fix the problem.

Unfortunately, I received no response to that report.

At this point, I'm left wondering whether:

A) My account has been shadowbanned without any explanation or apparent reason.

B) There's a serious bug affecting account visibility and message delivery that hasn't been properly investigated or addressed.

Neither possibility is reassuring

reviews.title: Basic features are blocked unless you pay
reviews.text:
This app has so much potential, but the way it locks basic features behind an expensive paywall is incredibly frustrating. Features that are completely normal and free on other dating apps require a subscription here, and it honestly makes the app feel cheap and unnecessarily restrictive.

For example, even Hinge lets you see who’s next in your feed by simply liking or passing on the current person. Bumpy makes something as basic as browsing potential matches feel unnecessarily complicated unless you’re willing to pay.

The translation feature is another major issue. For an app designed to connect people internationally, you’d think having a reliable translator would be a priority. Unfortunately, the translations are often so inaccurate that I’m genuinely hesitant to match with someone who speaks a language I don’t understand. But hey, they will give you a better translator, if YOU PAY. How are people supposed to build meaningful connections when they can’t even trust the translations? 

I understand that developers need to make money, and I have no problem with apps offering premium features. But there’s a difference between charging for genuinely enhanced experiences and deliberately restricting basic functionality to push people into paying.

When other dating apps offer these features for free, charging excessive amounts for them doesn’t make your app feel premium. It makes it feel greedy, poorly designed, and ultimately less enjoyable to use.

If two consenting adults meet on Bumpy and decide they want to exchange phone numbers and continue getting to know each other outside the app, why should that result in account deactivation?

Am I supposed to keep every relationship confined to Bumpy indefinitely? What happens when I meet someone who could potentially be marriage material and we naturally want to communicate by phone, text, or WhatsApp?

I understand protecting users from scams, harassment, spam, and inappropriate behavior. But voluntarily giving my own phone number to someone I’m interested in dating is a personal decision. If that violates Bumpy’s rules, then Bumpy needs to clearly explain exactly what rule was violated and why.

I was actively using the app, paying for a subscription, and getting to know people. Now my account is gone, and I’m left with no meaningful explanation.

Bumpy should provide transparency, tell me the specific guideline I violated, explain whether this was an automated or human decision, and give me a legitimate opportunity to appeal.

A dating app should help

reviews.title: DO NOT BUY THIS APP!
reviews.text:
I had a terrifying experience after using this app. Two years ago, in October 2024, while I was a senior in college and recovering from a difficult July breakup with my online British ex-boyfriend, I went on Bumpy and matched with a guy who claimed to be British. At first, it seemed okay. We exchanged our WhatsApp and followed each other on Instagram, but then things started to change.

He repeatedly pressured me to send intimate photos. After constant pressure, I sent one picture just to get him to stop. When he continued demanding more, I blocked him. Shortly afterward, he contacted me again and threatened to post the intimate photo online unless I paid him $600. He then confessed that he had catfished me and was actually from Pakistan.

The situation became so serious that I had to involve my parents, my college, campus police, and even the FBI. It was one of the most frightening experiences of my life.

I’m not saying the app itself committed this crime, but I encourage everyone to be extremely cautious when talking to strangers online. Verify who you’re speaking with, never let anyone pressure you into sending intimate images, and if someone threatens or blackmails you, do not pay them, please report it to law enforcement immediately.

This experience has made me think twice about using dating apps, and I would not recommend this one based on what happened to me. Do better, Bumpy. Do not let fake profiles into your app!

reviews.text:
I’ve been using Bumpy since January 2026, and I’ve genuinely enjoyed the app, which is why this recent change is so disappointing.

Removing the option to watch ads for additional likes is a huge step backwards. The feature was a fair balance. Free users could earn a few extra likes by watching ads, while Bumpy generated advertising revenue. It was a win-win for both users and the platform.

What’s even more disappointing is that this option has also been removed for Gold subscribers. People who are already paying for the app have now lost a feature they previously had access to, making the subscription feel like it’s offering less value than before.

Instead of making the experience better, this change makes the app feel more restrictive. It gives the impression that users are being pushed towards stricter limits without receiving anything in return.

Dating apps are incredibly competitive, and one of the reasons I appreciated Bumpy was that it offered users some flexibility. Removing features that people actively used is unlikely to improve the experience or encourage loyalty.

I really hope the team reconsiders this decision and restores the ability to earn extra likes by watching ads. It was a simple, user-friendly feature that benefited everyone, rewarded engagement, and helped make Bumpy stand out from other dating apps.

Usually, I get 20+ likes and consistent profile views daily. For the last week, my views have dropped to absolute ZERO. I am sending likes and comments daily and using paid Boosts, yet the app shows that not a single person has viewed my profile in 7 days. This is mathematically impossible for an active account, especially during a paid Boost.
I contacted support, but they gave me a canned response saying "everything is fine." This is a known issue. There are current Reddit threads where multiple users are reporting this exact same "ghosting" bug and receiving the same unhelpful replies from support.
This isn't a "bio" or "photo" issue; it’s a visibility/indexing failure. My profile is clearly not being served to the discovery stack. I am paying for a service (Boosts) that is providing zero impressions. Please have a technical specialist investigate why certain accounts are being hidden from the feed.

reviews.title: Misleading Premium Engagement, throttling your engagement based on subscription status
reviews.text:
I paid for a premium subscription twice to support the app and access full features. During both subscriptions, engagement on my profile was great until the final 2 days of my subscription — in one case, only 2 likes over two days. Which was a decrease from about 10 per day. 

Within 1–2 hours after my subscription expired this morning my like count jumped from approximately 28–29 to 92, all of which were locked behind a paywall prompting me to purchase again. Very suspicious to have such a massive increase in activity minutes after my subscription expired. 

I contacted support multiple times with detailed timestamps and numbers, and each response was vague, dismissive, and avoided the facts. They denied any mechanism to delay or manipulate activity, calling the spike a “coincidence,” despite the extremely unlikely timing.

This feels misleading and manipulative, making it impossible to trust the app as a paying customer. I will not pay for this service again, and I do not recommend it to anyone looking for fair, transparent engagement.

reviews.title: Fake/scam profiles
reviews.text: A good concept ruined by what plagues most other dating apps. And like those other apps, “photo verified” means nothing. If they are “photo verified” but not “location verified”, it is a fake profile. If they try to immediately move the chat to WhatsApp, it’s a fake profile. If they start a chat with you but have never looked at your profile, it’s a fake profile. If they refuse to do a video call in the app, it is definitely a fake profile. It’s sad that app developers allow and encourage fake profiles to be made, all because it makes them more money because these profiles “boost their numbers”, and you the consumer have to pay for a service to try to talk to someone who isn’t real. The developers have the means to stop this, they just choose not to because it would hurt their bottom line, and pass off responsibility to the consumer saying “you can report them”. We are not paying you to do YOUR job for you.

reviews.title: This app is fundamentally broken and has resulted in my account being unfairly suspended.
reviews.text:
The Main Problem: The built-in voice call feature is completely non-functional. It simply does not work, making it impossible to move a connection beyond basic texting on the platform itself.
For the past week, in an effort to actually use the connections I made, I was forced to provide external contact details (Instagram handles, Google Meet links) just to have a conversation—something the app claims to facilitate.
As a direct consequence of working around their own broken technology, my account was suspended for sharing external contact info. This is utterly hypocritical and unacceptable. The app penalized me for trying to use it effectively, only because their primary feature (voice calls) failed to function.
Fix your platform before punishing users for your technical shortcomings. I wasted time and energy only to be blocked. Do not download until this severe feature failure and policing policy is fixed.
